transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-06-10
- Start: 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~56 minutes
- Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Rachel Owens (CTO, SummitDocs), Samir Patel (SWE), Tina Gomez (PM)

Summary:
High-level migration demo focused on mapping SummitDocs' existing OpenAI-based integration to Redwood API. Covered parity for completions/chat, embeddings, function calling, streaming behavior, rate limits and batching, and enterprise controls (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Customer asked about latency/cost tradeoffs and Dedicated vs Hosted. Agreed next steps: share parity sheet, run benchmark on Dedicated, provide trial keys and sample repo.

Topics:
- API parity and parameter mapping (model names, temperature, top_p, n, stop, max_tokens)
- Chat->Completions differences and function calling mapping
- Embeddings endpoint differences and vector dimensions
- Streaming & SSE vs Redwood streaming socket behavior
- Batching, KV cache, and cost-saving features (Optimize suggestions)
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, VPC, SSO (SAML), audit logs
- Dedicated (reserved) vs Hosted tradeoffs

Action items (recap in call):
- Ava to send parity spreadsheet and sample code snippets
- Liam to set up benchmark run and baseline scripts
- Customer to share current usage metrics and prompts

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava: Hi everybody, thanks for joining — this is Ava from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. With me is Liam, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Rachel: Good, thanks. Rachel here. We are excited to see how close Redwood can get to our current OpenAI setup, and what the migration lift looks like.
[00:12] Samir: Yep, Samir — we own the backend that calls OpenAI, mostly completions and embeddings, some streaming in a few features.
[00:18] Tina: And I'm Tina, PM on the docs product. Our main asks are parity and cost predictability.
[00:24] Liam: Awesome. Quick agenda: we'll run through the Redwood API compatibility layer, model mapping, demo a few calls (chat/completions, function calling, embeddings), then talk about Dedicated vs Hosted and security. We'll leave time for questions.
[00:33] Rachel: Sounds good. One quick thing — our token spend is ~1.2B tokens/month, variances up to 30% seasonally. Latency matters for live editing flows, but we can tolerate up to ~250ms P95 for most requests.
[00:45] Ava: Great context, thanks. That actually helps with the Dedicated discussion.
[00:48] Liam: Alright I'll share my screen — bear with me while I open the Redwood Console. (screen share)
[00:58] Liam: So this is the Console, top left you can see the model catalog — we surface verified profiles for models, including map to common upstream names like 'gpt-4o' equivalents and open models. For migration we generally map OpenAI models to Redwood-hosted variants; we also keep a compatibility shim for standard request params.
[01:18] Samir: When you say 'compatibility shim', do you mean we can keep the same request body for the most part? We have a lot of wrappers in production.
[01:25] Liam: Yes, for the most part. For the basic fields — model, prompt/messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop, n — the mapping is straightforward. For chat function calling, Redwood supports the same function schema, but with a slight variant in how we return a function_call object in streaming mode. We'll share exact examples in the parity sheet.
[01:47] Rachel: Do you support streaming function call partials? Our UI relies on early partials to start rendering.
[01:54] Liam: We do. Redwood streams tokens and also stream function call events; in our SDK we surface an onFunctionChunk callback. The SSE stream format is slightly different than OpenAI's chunk structure — sometimes different names in the envelope — so you will need a tiny adapter, but it's at the client layer only.
[02:12] Tina: Great — that was one of our biggest worries. About embeddings: we use ada-embedding-002 today, 1536 dims, and store vectors in our existing vector DB. What are Redwood's embeddings dimensions and similarity?
[02:25] Liam: We host several embeddings models. For migration, we typically match on dimension and semantic behavior. For example our rwd-embed-1536 has compatible dimensions. Similarity scores are comparable but you should re-run a small eval to verify thresholds. We'll include a mapping for the exact model you use.
[02:41] Samir: Any changes required on the DB side? Indexing vector dims is fine, but do you return cosine vs dot product scores?
[02:49] Liam: We return raw vectors; we also provide a scoring utility we share in the sample repo. Whether you use cosine or dot is up to your DB — Redwood doesn't force a specific score.
[02:59] Rachel: Can you talk about rate limits and bursting? We have spiky traffic patterns.
[03:05] Ava: Sure. Hosted API has fair-use limits that can be increased. With Dedicated you get reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput; you can configure burst pools for sudden spikes. If you hit capacity, routing can fall back to a lower-cost model or a hosted pool based on policy.
[03:24] Samir: How about billing — is Dedicated flat monthly and Hosted per-token?
[03:29] Ava: Exactly. Hosted is usage-based (per token / per embedding unit). Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly, with overage rules if you exceed. We'll share pricing examples in the spreadsheet.
[03:40] Tina: What about batching and KV cache — can you parameterize those? We rely a lot on prefix caching for chat continuity.
[03:47] Liam: Yes, our runtime exposes smart batching and KV cache behavior. On the API you can set cache hints and session keys; the runtime uses those to decide whether to reuse KV cache. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations for batching and cache TTLs per route to reduce cost.
[04:04] Rachel: Nice. Security — SSO and KMS — we need SAML SSO and customer-managed keys for Dedicated.
[04:11] Ava: We support SAML SSO for the Console, and for Private/Dedicated we integrate with KMS/HSM for envelope encryption. We'll send the SOC2/ISO certs and the KMS integration guide.
[04:20] Samir: Do you keep logs of requests? We need audit logs with redaction options.
[04:25] Liam: We provide audit logs and optional redaction at ingest. In Dedicated you control retention policies and where logs live.
[04:32] Tina: Can we see a quick demo of a request? Even pseudo code is fine.
[04:36] Liam: Sure — I'll do a quick live curl vs Redwood SDK example. (types)
[04:45] Liam: Example OpenAI call first: curl to api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with messages, model, temperature. Now Redwood: POST to api.redwood.ai/v1/completions (or /v1/chat for the chat-style) with almost same payload. Here's the parity snippet. Model name is rwd-gpt-4o-equivalent or rwd-gpt-3.5 for the gpt-3.5 family.
[05:07] Samir: Can you paste that snippet in chat so we can copy?
[05:11] Liam: Yep — done. (pastes link) Sorry auto transcribed link: https://redwood.ai/docs/migration (note: placeholder)
[05:20] Rachel: What about the function calling differences you mentioned earlier?
[05:24] Liam: The main difference is event names in streaming. OpenAI sends delta.function_call.name/content in chunks; Redwood streams 'fn_call' events with name and partial args. The SDK normalizes that for you. If you're using raw SSE parsing today you'll need a small adapter — maybe 20 lines.
[05:43] Tina: Ok. Regarding embeddings: do you have a bulk embeddings API? We do batched upserts nightly.
[05:49] Liam: Yes, we support bulk embeddings up to configurable batch sizes; we also have parallelization helpers in the SDK to maximize throughput and avoid throttles.
[05:58] Samir: Latency: you mentioned 250ms P95 tolerance. Can Redwood hit that for chat in Hosted?
[06:05] Liam: For short sequences and smaller models yes; for larger context windows or bigger models P95 will be higher. That's where Dedicated helps — pinned GPU capacity and lower queuing. We'll bench with your traffic shape to show expected P95.
[06:21] Rachel: We also want to ensure prompt engineering results stay the same — no surprising tokenization differences.
[06:27] Liam: Good point. Tokenization is consistent for the hosted model family that maps to OpenAI equivalence; we recommend validating with a small validation set. We'll include tokenizer check scripts.
[06:39] Ava: Quick Q for SummitDocs: Do you use function calling heavily for data fetching (like call to your metadata service) or is it mostly for tool orchestration?
[06:48] Samir: Mostly tool orchestration — we call a metadata microservice and then transform responses into UI components. Latency on that path is critical because we scrape the partials to show progressive UI.
[06:58] Liam: That's a good match for streaming function partials — we'll prioritize that in the benchmark.
[07:04] Tina: What's the effort to switch SDKs? We have a thin wrapper layer, but it's used by many services.
[07:11] Ava: Most customers write a 1-2 day adapter in the worst case — mostly import path changes and small streaming adapters. Some customers drop-in replace with a tiny shim that rewrites host and model names. We'll include a sample shim in the repo.
[07:25] Rachel: Do you support both JSON-RPC style and REST? We use REST.
[07:29] Liam: REST is the default. We also have SDKs in Node/Python/Go that wrap streaming nicely.
[07:35] Samir: Let's talk about fallbacks — if Dedicated goes down or is saturated how does Redwood route?
[07:42] Liam: Smart routing can fail over to hosted pools, or to a smaller cheaper model variant. You configure policies in the Console: region, latency, and cost preferences.
[07:53] Tina: Any customers who've migrated from OpenAI at this scale (1B tokens/month)?
[07:58] Ava: Yes, a few lateral customers — we can share anonymized case study metrics on cost reductions and latency improvements. I'll include those refs.
[08:07] Rachel: One more: encryption at rest — who manages keys for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[08:13] Liam: Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default; Dedicated/Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. We'll send the KMS integration doc.
[08:21] Samir: Ok, thanks. Can we run a short live sample request so we can see logs and trace?
[08:27] Liam: Sure — I'll trigger a simple chat call and show the trace view. (executes)
[08:36] Liam: Here's the request in the Console trace — you can see token breakdown, latency per stage, and cost estimate. Note the per-token cost estimate appears here for Hosted; for Dedicated you get utilization metrics instead.
[08:51] Rachel: That trace view looks useful. Are traces linked back to audit logs?
[08:55] Liam: Yes, you can link traces to audit entries and tie them to session IDs. In Dedicated you export logs to your SIEM.
[09:03] Tina: For the benchmarking, how long do you typically need? Can we do a 2-hour run simulating peak?
[09:09] Liam: Two hours is fine. We'll want representative traffic (Samir to share token distribution), and we'll provision the Dedicated slot. We'll capture P95, throughput, and cost per token.
[09:21] Ava: I'll take the action to schedule that once Samir sends the traffic profile.
[09:25] Samir: Will do.
[09:27] Rachel: One operational question — how do you handle model updates/rollouts so we don't get a regression in quality?
[09:33] Liam: We support pinning model versions per route and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallbacks if top-k evals fail. Our Optimize product monitors quality regressions by running your prompt set and alerts on drift.
[09:46] Tina: Can you show how to pin a model in the Console quickly?
[09:50] Liam: (navigates) Here — per-route config, you can select exact model version and rollout percentage. You can also attach a prompt test suite that runs on deploy.
[09:59] Rachel: This is great. Any blockers on data residency? We need EU region only for some workloads.
[10:05] Ava: We have regional deployments and can pin routes to EU-only. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy in your cloud region.
[10:13] Samir: Ok, last big question: cost. What reductions can we expect?
[10:19] Ava: It depends on workload, but from similar migrations customers saw 20-40% unit cost reductions by switching models, enabling caching, and better batching. We'll give a modeled estimate based on your data.
[10:33] Tina: Sounds promising.
[10:36] Rachel: Let's look at the parity spreadsheet you mentioned.
[10:39] Liam: I pasted a link in the meeting chat — it contains a column-by-column mapping: OpenAI param -> Redwood param -> notes. For example, 'max_tokens' is identical, 'stop' arrays map 1:1, 'n' maps to parallel completions, and chat/messages map to our /chat endpoint. Function calling differences are documented in a separate sheet.
[11:03] Samir: Will you include example error codes? We want to map retries and idempotency.
[11:09] Liam: Yes — we'll include the error mapping and recommended retry semantics for 429, 5xx, and rate-limited scenarios.
[11:17] Ava: Switching gears — any questions about the Console or Optimize?
[11:21] Tina: How does Optimize surface suggestions? Is it a box in the Console?
[11:26] Liam: Optimize runs automated audits and shows suggestions per route: batching size, cache TTL, quantization profile. It ranks recommendations by estimated cost savings and risk.
[11:39] Rachel: We use quantized models for some lower-cost endpoints; does Redwood support quantized inference?
[11:45] Liam: Yes — the runtime supports quantized kernels and we can recommend quantization for specific models. Dedicated supports Q8/Q4 variants depending on hardware.
[11:55] Samir: Any differences in embeddings quality when using quantized models?
[12:00] Liam: Minor — we recommend evaluating with your QA set. For many workloads the embedding quality is preserved.
[12:06] Tina: Ok. I think that's most of my list.
[12:10] Rachel: Me too. Can we recap next steps and owners?
[12:14] Ava: Sure — recap: Ava sends parity sheet, price examples, and SOC2/KMS docs by Thursday (2025-06-12). Liam prepares benchmark scripts and provisions Dedicated slot for a 2-hour run (target by 2025-06-17). Samir shares token distributions and sample prompts by Friday (2025-06-13). We will provide a trial API key and sample repo.
[12:36] Samir: Sounds good.
[12:38] Tina: Thanks everyone.
[12:41] Ava: Thanks — we'll follow up in email and attach the repo. Bye.
[12:45] Meeting end (screenshare stopped).

Notes on transcription quality: some transcription artifacts — SDK names sometimes transcribed as 'red would', 'r d wood', or 'g p t' etc. We will include clean links in follow-up.
